summary: Working in philosophy, Japanology, and history and archaeology, Ernest Fenollosa studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo Fine Arts School, and Boston's Museum of Fine Arts.

An archaeologist and Indologist, Ernest John Henry Mackay studied at Bristol Grammar School and earned degrees from the University of Bristol. From 1919 to 1922, he served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Palestine.

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. Educated at Saint-Sulpice and the Collège de France, studying under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Collège de France.

Philosopher Ernest Sosa studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as a professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Historian and archaeologist Ernst Curtius studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at the University of Göttingen (1855–1867) and Humboldt University of Berlin, and directed the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

Working in linguistics and history and archaeology, Ernst Förstemann studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He held library posts at the Fürst zu Stolberg-Wernigerodesche Bibliothek and the Dresden library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, completing his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held positions at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), the University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems.

Ernst Gombrich was an art historian who studied at the University of Vienna. He worked at the Warburg Institute starting in 1936, later serving as its director from 1959 to 1976, and held a post at the University of London.

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at the universities of Berlin, Bonn, and Tübingen, learning under Albrecht Weber. He worked at the British Museum from 1866 and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.
Ernst Haeckel studied at the Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1854 to 1857. He later held a post at the University of Jena from around 1862 to 1909.

Ernst Johann Eitel worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, completing MA and PhD degrees at the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and as a lecturer and professor at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Kuhn studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Heidelberg under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Halle, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, before becoming a professor at the University of Munich (1877–1917).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Leumann studied in Zurich, Geneva, Berlin, Leipzig, and Strasbourg under Albrecht Weber and Friedrich Haag. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford and held professorships at the University of Strasbourg and University of Freiburg.

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague and the teacher examination commission in Prague. He later held an academic post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1948 to 1963.

Indologist and Tibetologist Ernst Steinkellner studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He served as associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1971) and as director at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Indologist and linguist Ernst Trumpp studied under Rudolf von Roth at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen. He worked at the East India Company, became a Privatdozent at the University of Tübingen, and served as professor at the University of Munich (~1873–1885).

Ernst Waldschmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Kiel and Berlin under Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, Heinrich Lüders, and others. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin and held the Indology chair at Göttingen (1936–1965).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Windisch completed his doctorate at Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg and Strasbourg, and served as a professor at Leipzig.
Linguist Ernst Zinn held academic appointments at the University of Hamburg from around 1947 to 1951, Saarland University from 1951 to 1956, and the University of Tübingen from around 1951 to 1978.

Sinologist Erwin Rousselle studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and Darmstadt under teachers including Max Walleser. He held posts at Peking University, Tsinghua University, the Sino-Indian Institute at Yenching University, and Goethe University Frankfurt.
